column8: ★★ PARTIAL SELF-CORRECTION. On 7/24, with only DHI (20.7%) and PHM (25.0%) in hand, HOMER concluded margin crush was COHORT-SPECIFIC and that scale builders were successfully defending. Six more Q2 prints revise that: NVR -230bps, MTH -280bps, GRBK -150bps, DFH 16.5->14.2 — YoY compression is now visible essentially ACROSS the sector, including at scale builders. WHAT SURVIVES: the LEVEL dispersion is huge and cohort-driven (GRBK 29.8% vs DFH 14.2% = 15.6pp in the same quarter), and entry-level/Sun-Belt-weighted names remain the crushed end. BETTER FRAME: "compression universal, level dispersion cohort-driven, and order growth is PURCHASED." THE MECHANISM, which is the real finding: every builder that grew orders did it on a FALLING ASP (GRBK -11.9%, DFH -8.9%, NVR -5%), while the one that held price (MTH) printed -9% orders and cut guidance. Cancellation rates IMPROVED almost everywhere (MHO 13->8%, DFH 11.1%) — consistent with buyers being CLEARED AT PRICE rather than walking away. CRL-23 (CARL's) UNCHANGED: DHI 20.7% and PHM 25.0% remain far above the <=17.5%/<=22.0% triggers, but the sector-wide direction is now compression, which raises the prior on the FY27 resolvers.
